newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends down in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends down in thin trade.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar finished lower on Saturday amid fears that the United States might raise interest rates, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.545 to the dollar against Friday's T$27.537 close.
Turnover through dealers was a scanty US$33.5 million.
"News reports that the United States may raise its interest rates and the Taiwan's pork export ban had created some pressure and pulled down the local currency," said one dealer.
Taiwan on Thursday announced that it was banning exports of fresh and frozen pork due to an outbreak of the deadly and contagious foot and mouth disease.
The ban is expected to cut overall exports by some 1.5 percent and reduce the island's trade surplus, dealers said.
Dealers also attributed the local dollar's weakness to quarter-end U.S. dollar demand and a response to the strength of the U.S. dollar overseas.
A T$27.50-27.55 range was seen for next week.
